product: What Rigetti actually sells today is full-stack superconducting quantum hardware and access, not a software subscription: on-premises 9-qubit Novera QPUs and 36-qubit to 108-qubit Cepheus-class systems (Cepheus-1-108Q is built from twelve tiled 9-qubit chiplets and ships with Rigetti's own control electronics), plus cloud access via Rigetti Quantum Cloud Services (QCS) and collaborative research and professional services. On suppliers, Rigetti is vertically integrated for the critical input - it designs and manufactures its quantum chiplets in-house at Fab-1 in Fremont, the industry's first dedicated quantum device manufacturing facility - so it does not depend on an external foundry for its processors, but the Q2 2026 10-Q shows the remaining external dependency is cryogenics and control hardware: it describes future capex to purchase additional dilution refrigeration equipment, and the three funded CHIPS R&D projects are precisely (i) compressing readout electronics into an integrated miniaturized package, (ii) expanding cryogenic capacity by orders of magnitude with a new cryostat architecture and (iii) developing high-connectivity chip fabrication. Watching supplier terms, accounts payable jumped to $14.001M at 6/30/26 from $3.488M at 12/31/25 and H1 2026 purchases of property and equipment rose to $16.404M from $8.214M, a large step-up in procurement and capex commitments consistent with the cryostat and fab build-out; the 10-Q also notes purchase commitments may change based on expected timing of order fulfillment from suppliers, and no supplier is named or disclosed as concentrated.
demand: Demand is moving with mix and with unit count off a very small base rather than with price: Q2 2026 revenue was $5.138M versus $1.801M a year earlier (+185%) and H1 2026 was $9.538M versus $3.273M (+191%), which the 10-Q attributes mainly to higher sales of 9-qubit Novera systems and related products. Customer composition has rotated hard away from government research contracts - government entities were 18.0% of Q2 2026 revenue (22.2% of H1 2026) versus 91.7% of Q2 2025 and 90.7% of H1 2025 - toward one-off on-premises system purchases by universities, national laboratories, quantum computing centers and foreign buyers (C-DAC India $8.4M order in January 2026, the UK National Quantum Computing Centre 36-qubit system, the Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center TangleLab Novera funded by an NSF grant, and the HPE hybrid quantum-classical collaboration). Concentration and churn are the live risks: Customer A alone was 64% of Q2 2026 revenue (34% for H1 2026) with Customer C at 16%, accounts-receivable concentration shifted to Customer C at 43% and Customer B at 21% at 6/30/26, remaining performance obligations were only about $2.7M at 6/30/26, and management warns revenue timing will vary because deliveries of QPUs, systems and QCaaS are lumpy.
pricing_power: Weak - Rigetti cannot currently raise prices without risking volume. The 11.3-point gross margin expansion (31.4% in Q2 2025 to 42.6% in Q2 2026) came from mix, not price: the 10-Q states a significant portion of Q2 2026 revenue was on-premises 9-qubit Novera systems and related products, and that these carry a higher gross margin profile than collaborative research and professional services, while explicitly warning that cost of revenue and gross profit percentage will vary with the composition of revenue and with variability in the pricing and terms of sales. Buyers are government labs, universities and research centers buying with grant and budget money, and the September 2026 government deal shows the direction of leverage: to secure $100M of CHIPS funding the company issued 7,739,938 shares at an implied $12.92, conceding equity (about 2.3% dilution) rather than commanding better terms, and the award is milestone-gated with clawback rights if milestones are missed.
competition: Rigetti competes as a gate-based superconducting pure-play against much larger superconducting players (IBM, Google), against different modalities in IonQ and Quantinuum (trapped ion) and PsiQuantum and Atom Computing (neutral atoms), and against D-Wave in annealing; its differentiation claim is gate speed of 50-70 nanoseconds, about 10,000 times faster than trapped-ion and 100 times faster than neutral-atom systems, plus chiplet-based tiling. If Rigetti is right, the specific losers are the trapped-ion and neutral-atom incumbents whose fidelity and coherence edge is offset by far slower gates, and IBM and Google to the extent chiplet tiling scales more cheaply than monolithic fabrication - but with only $541.3M of cash, no debt, about $5.1M of quarterly revenue and a roughly $5.5B market capitalization, Rigetti is today the smallest balance sheet in that field, so share is still mostly moving to IBM, Google and IonQ on commercial deals while Rigetti's wins are grant-funded deployments. Second- and third-order beneficiaries if the superconducting trend continues are dilution-refrigerator and cryostat makers (Bluefors, Oxford Instruments), helium-3 and cryogenic component suppliers, cryo-CMOS readout and RF test-and-measurement vendors (Zurich Instruments, Keysight, Rohde and Schwarz), HPC integrators and partners such as HPE, national-laboratory and university testbeds, and quantum-themed indices or ETFs that gain a pure-play superconducting constituent.
team: Leadership changed within the last 90 days: on August 18, 2026 David Rivas moved from Chief Technology Officer to the newly created Chief Operating Officer role, with his base salary raised to $440,000 per the 8-K, and Andrew Bestwick (Senior Vice President, Quantum Systems, at Rigetti since 2015 and architect of the Cepheus-class multi-chip systems) was appointed Chief Technology Officer; both report to President and CEO Dr. Subodh Kulkarni, with Jeffrey Bertelsen as CFO. The company also created a dedicated Systems Delivery organization that Rivas will lead across fabrication operations, systems delivery, software engineering, applications, business development, government programs, supply chain and facilities, which management justified by increased demand for on-premises 9-qubit Novera through 108-qubit Cepheus-class deployments. Separately, director Dr. Ray Johnson resigned from the board effective August 28, 2026, with the company stating his decision was not due to any disagreement, so one board seat turned over alongside the C-suite reorganization.
market_strategy: Management's stated plan for the next twelve months is to convert Rigetti into a systems delivery company and keep funding the processor roadmap: stand up the new dedicated Systems Delivery organization under the new COO, fulfil the on-premises 108-qubit Cepheus-1-108Q order for C-DAC in Bengaluru in H2 2026 and keep shipping Novera and 108-qubit systems to universities, national laboratories and quantum centers, push Cepheus-1-108Q from its current roughly 99.9% median single-qubit and 99.1% median two-qubit gate fidelity and 60 nanosecond gate speed toward a 99.5% median two-qubit fidelity target, and pursue the roughly 1,000-qubit, 99.9% two-qubit, sub-50-nanosecond roadmap over about a three-year horizon while executing the three milestone-gated CHIPS R&D projects and spending up to $100M in the UK over several years. What changed in the last 90 days that was not knowable a year earlier is that the May 2026 letter of intent became a signed definitive Other Transaction Agreement on September 4, 2026 giving up to $100M under the CHIPS Act in exchange for a minority, non-controlling U.S. Department of Commerce equity stake of 7,739,938 shares at $12.92, with a five-year period of performance, foreign-entity and domestic-production restrictions, march-in and government licence rights over developed IP and clawback of disbursed funds if milestones are missed; the other 90-day change is the COO/CTO reorganization and the board resignation. The only genuinely this-week dated item is that Q3 2026 earnings are now algorithm-estimated for November 9, 2026, and that RGTI closed September 24 at $16.50, up 3.09% within a 52-week range of $12.53 to $58.15; note Rigetti issues no revenue guidance, so the strategy is judged on technological milestones and deployment announcements, not on guided numbers.
bull: Rigetti's $100M Department of Commerce equity stake and CHIPS Other Transaction Agreement (award 2026-09-04) has its first $43.9M tranche becoming available around the award date, funding a revenue base that grew +185% y/y (Q2) off a small starting point, driven by 9-qubit Novera and 108-qubit system sales; an on-prem 108-qubit Cepheus-1-108Q system ships to C-DAC Bengaluru in H2 2026, and reported fidelities (~99.9% median single-qubit, ~99.1% two-qubit) support the technical roadmap. This is the thematic book's own 'supports (policy)' quantum pick.
bear: The revenue base is still tiny ($5.1M in Q2) so a 185% growth rate is not yet meaningful at scale, and government revenue collapsed from 91.7% of Q2 2025 revenue to just 18.0% of Q2 2026 -- which could read as successful commercial diversification (C-DAC, universities) or as a shrinking captive government book not yet replaced at scale; the filings don't resolve which. The two subsequent CHIPS tranches ($29.9M, $26.2M) are milestone-gated, not guaranteed, and analyst views are split (B. Riley Buy $35 vs Northland Hold $20 vs TD Cowen Hold with no target) -- less extreme than QUBT's $10-$32 spread but the same disagreement pattern this program treats as a caution (SS17), not a reason to buy the ~31% implied upside.
falsifier: If the 10-Q/8-K terms show the government's $100M as a grant/award rather than an actual equity stake -- the book's own stated falsifier for this position -- or if government revenue keeps shrinking without commercial/international orders replacing it at scale, that falsifies the policy-backed thesis; milestone tranches actually releasing on schedule and government revenue stabilizing would confirm it.
